original_question: Assume X satisfies Ufin(O,Omega). For each continuous image Y of X in N^N, define G = { g in N^N : there exist k and f1,...,fk in Y with g <=* max{f1,...,fk} }. Must G satisfy Ufin(O,Omega)?
target_in_paper: §12, Problem 12.1 ([66]) in §12 (Additional problems and other special sets of reals), together with the immediately preceding sentence that quantifies over continuous images Y of X in N^N.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact official target almost verbatim: it has the right hypothesis Ufin(O,Ω), the right continuous-image setting Y⊆N^N, the right finitely-max-generated family G, and the right preservation question asking whether G must itself satisfy Ufin(O,Ω).
missing_details: The paper’s ambient class is sets of real numbers (subspaces of R), not arbitrary topological spaces.
The quantifier over Y should be explicit in a stand-alone version: for every continuous image Y of X into N^N.
N^N is being used as Baire space with its usual product topology.
The set G is considered with the subspace topology inherited from N^N.
The relation g<=*h means g(n)≤h(n) for all but finitely many n.
The expression max{f1,...,fk} means the pointwise maximum function n↦max_i fi(n).
The integer k should be specified as a positive integer.
To be fully stand-alone, Ufin(O,Ω) should be defined: for every sequence of nontrivial open covers with no finite subcover, one can choose finite subfamilies whose unions form an ω-cover.
The paper’s convention is that covers are nontrivial, i.e. the whole space is not itself a member of the cover.
An ω-cover should be defined explicitly: every finite subset of the space is contained in some member of the cover.
The nearby context also records the known weaker fact that this G is not comeager in N^N; that is motivation for the problem, but not part of the question itself.
refined_question: Let X⊆R be a set of reals satisfying Ufin(O,Ω): whenever (U_n)_{n∈N} is a sequence of nontrivial open covers of X, none containing a finite subcover, there exist finite subfamilies F_n⊆U_n such that {∪F_n:n∈N} is an ω-cover of X (that is, every finite subset of X is contained in some ∪F_n). Is it true that for every continuous image Y of X in Baire space N^N (with the product topology), the subspace G_Y={g∈N^N: there exist a positive integer k and f_1,...,f_k∈Y with g<=*max{f_1,...,f_k}} also satisfies Ufin(O,Ω), where g<=*h means g(n)≤h(n) for all but finitely many n and max{f_1,...,f_k}(n)=max_{1≤i≤k} f_i(n)?
justification: The draft is aiming at the labeled Problem 12.1 in §12. The only substantial hidden point in the paper’s official wording is that the variable Y is introduced in the immediately preceding sentence, so a stand-alone reformulation must restore the universal quantifier over continuous images Y⊆N^N. Section 1 supplies the meanings of Ufin(A,B), ω-cover, and the convention that covers are nontrivial, and the introduction states that the chapter restricts attention to sets of real numbers. I therefore kept the question narrowly faithful to Problem 12.1 rather than drifting to neighboring questions about Ufin(O,Ω) elsewhere in the paper.
